title: Describing the world
subtitle: arid, tundra, indigenous, at the forefront
summary: Describe a country the way a geography text does - its climate, vegetation, farming, industry and people - with the exact words each field uses.

lesson.heading: Climate
lesson.text: **Rainfall** is the amount of rain that falls in, say, a month or a year. Land that is **arid** is dry, and a region **prone to** something tends to have that negative characteristic. A **drought** is a long period without rain.

examples.text: **Rainfall** in the south-east can be extremely high in the wet season.
The northern part of the country is **arid** and **prone to drought** during the dry season.
The river delta is **prone to** catastrophic flooding on a regular basis.

lesson.heading: Vegetation
rows: an area in the far north with no trees and permanently frozen ground
the dense coniferous forest south of the tundra
evergreen trees that produce cones and stay in leaf all year
trees that lose their leaves in winter
flat grasslands in Canada and the northern USA
the equivalent grasslands in Asia and in South America
lesson.note: More than 30% of Canada lies inside the Arctic Circle, where the land can stay frozen for up to nine months of the year and vegetation is limited.

lesson.heading: Agriculture
lesson.text: A **crop** is what a farmer grows and **harvests**. **Cereals** are types of grass cultivated to produce a grain - rice, wheat or maize. Rice is planted in flooded **paddy fields**. To **tend** animals is to take care of them.

examples.text: Rice is the main **crop** grown in the south of China, planted in flooded **paddy fields**.
A good year can see two crops of rice and one of vegetables **harvested**.
Farmers **harvest** a single crop of **cereals** and, in addition, **tend** sheep and cattle.
One can often see local shepherds **tending** large flocks of sheep on the hillsides.

left.label: A developed nation
left.text: One with a modern, industrial economy. It has large **manufacturing** industries - producing goods in large numbers - and may be **at the forefront** of a field, that is, in an important leading position.
examples: France is home to large **manufacturing**, steel and chemical industries.
The country is **at the forefront** of technology and engineering.
Its sizeable nuclear industry **generates** a significant proportion of the nation's electrical power.

right.label: A developing nation
right.text: One that is poor and does not have a modern, industrial economy. Developed countries provide **aid** to them.
examples: Like many developed countries, France provides a lot of help and **aid** to **developing** countries.

lesson.heading: Population
lesson.text: People **descended from** someone are related to a person who lived in the past: our **ancestors** are our relatives from earlier times, and we are their **descendants**. **Indigenous** peoples exist naturally in that place, unlike **migrants**, who move to live somewhere else and **settle** there - make their homes.

examples.text: Some Brazilians are **descended from indigenous** tribes, others from the Portuguese.
Many Brazilians have African **ancestors** brought over in the 17th century as slaves.
During the 20th century, large numbers of European **migrants settled** in the south.

lesson.note: An emigrant leaves a country; an immigrant moves into one. Migrant covers both, and also people moving within their own country.

lesson.heading: Useful collocations
lesson.note: Paddy goes only with field - there is no such thing as a paddy forest or a paddy crop.

lesson.text: Ancestors look backwards and descendants look forwards: your ancestors came from France, and you are their descendant.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each collocation.
Which noun does each word go with?
I believe my ___ came to Britain from France in the 17th century.
exercises.explanation: Ancestors are relatives from earlier times; we are our ancestors' descendants.

exercises.prompt: Many ___ left Russia for France after the Revolution in 1917.
exercises.explanation: An emigrant is someone who leaves a country.

exercises.prompt: The USA has traditionally welcomed ___ from all over the world.
exercises.explanation: An immigrant is someone who moves to live in a country.

exercises.prompt: Some Scots are said to be the ___ of 16th century Spanish sailors shipwrecked off the Scottish coast.
exercises.explanation: Descendants are the people related to someone who lived in the past.

exercises.prompt: Recently, the country's economy has suffered a decline in ___ industry.
exercises.explanation: Manufacturing industry produces goods in large numbers.

exercises.prompt: The university has long been at the ___ of agricultural science.
exercises.explanation: To be at the forefront of a field is to be in an important leading position in it.

exercises.prompt: In the late 18th century, migrants ___ in the uncultivated lands towards the north.
exercises.explanation: To settle somewhere is to make your home there.

exercises.prompt: In the extremely dry southern provinces, ___ is sparse.
exercises.explanation: Vegetation is the general word for plant life.

exercises.prompt: In the cold northern regions, the landscape consists mostly of permanently frozen ground with no trees. What is this called?
exercises.explanation: Tundra is the treeless area in the north with permanently frozen ground; taiga is the coniferous forest further south.

exercises.prompt: The tribes that have always existed naturally in the eastern jungles are ___ peoples.
exercises.explanation: Indigenous means existing naturally in that place.

exercises.prompt: The flat grasslands of the northern USA experienced a severe ___ last year.
exercises.explanation: A drought is a long period without rain; those grasslands are called the prairies.

exercises.statement: Deciduous trees are in leaf all year round, while coniferous trees lose their leaves in winter.
exercises.explanation: It is the other way round: coniferous trees are evergreen, and deciduous trees lose their leaves in winter.

exercises.statement: A country prone to flooding tends to suffer from it regularly.
exercises.explanation: Correct - prone to means tending to have a particular negative characteristic.

exercises.prompt: Put this sentence about China in order.
exercises.answer: The rice is planted in flooded paddy fields
exercises.explanation: Paddy fields are fields planted with rice growing in water.
